selection: Five mineral species and two distinct spent-catalyst resources extend the corpus. Florencite-(La) retains bounded identity/composition evidence; monazite-(La) adds a La-specific abiotic synthesis arm without importing Nd measurements. Hydroboracite preserves separate thermal and pressure experiments. Metatorbernite and metazeunerite separate natural air/vacuum observations from synthetic sealed-capillary behavior. The two catalyst resources distinguish leaching, retained residues and isolated products. No constituent criticality or unverified microbial mechanism is inherited.

source_issues.body:
The new `data/records/hydroboracite.yaml` records two distinct pressure arms and retains discrepancies in the original 2026 source. It does not adopt a single exact transition pressure or the deposited calculated densities. This issue tracks external evidence clarification; it is not an assertion that the qualified record is currently defective.

Evidence: [Comboni et al. (2026), DOI 10.1007/s00269-026-01339-x](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00269-026-01339-x), the [institutional manuscript](https://air.unimi.it/retrieve/d1a62dd8-230d-4e02-91d4-1823aa222c6e/hydroboracite_08-01-2026-unmarked.pdf), Table 1 on pp. 10–11, Results p. 12, Conclusions pp. 17–18, and all three publisher-linked CIFs.

- Table 1's last starting-phase/first high-pressure points are 14.40(5)/14.72(5) GPa for the first crystal and 14.08(5)/14.51(5) GPa for the second. Abstract, Results and Conclusions instead summarize different intervals. The reported 0.9(6)% volume difference combines points from different crystals; it is not a paired change in one crystal.
- Every CIF has `_cell_formula_units_Z = 1`, while atom-site multiplicities × occupancies give Ca2Mg2B12O34, two non-hydrogen formula units. The CIF cell metrics match first-arm starting-phase points at 0.32, 14.40 and 7.35 GPa in file order. These files do not provide a solved hydroboracite-II structure. Their calculated density fields need source clarification before reuse.
- Hydrogen positions were omitted, full crystal chemistry was unavailable, and the high-pressure structure and space group remain unresolved. Those limits must remain explicit even if metadata are corrected.

Acceptance requires a corrected publisher/source artifact or sufficiently documented original per-crystal data that resolves the stated intervals and the CIF formula-unit/density metadata. Preserve both experimental arms, identify the corrected artifact/version and checksum, and append curation history plus a new independent review for any changed accepted claims. Do not silently repair deposited metadata or infer a recovered crystalline product.

The 2026-10-15 bounded search found no relevant correction/retraction, and Crossref had no `update-to` relation; this is not proof none exists. The 277-issue all-state title/body inventory (comments excluded) had no hydroboracite/DOI match. Source acquisition and the exact contradictions are documented in `research/sources/round104-borates/20261015T221506Z-source-investigation.{json,md}`. No author contact or source correction has been performed.

source_issues.body:
Two new owners, `data/records/metatorbernite.yaml` and `data/records/metazeunerite.yaml`, deliberately separate natural and synthetic thermal experiments and preserve inconsistent source wording. This issue tracks external evidence clarification, not a defect requiring invention of a corrected temperature.

In [Nazarchuk et al. (2023)](https://doi.org/10.3390/cryst13121688), mixed pristine/partly dehydrated metatorbernite is assigned 313/463 K in Section 3.2 but 303/473 K in Section 4. Figure 5c-d misnames metazeunerite as metatorbernite, gives a 93 K start versus the 100 K methods boundary, and does not resolve whether its sample 2 is German 2a or Russian 2b. Article-cited deposits 2307946-2307947 were not retrieved because the authority service returned an access notice.

In [Kulaszewska et al. (2019)](https://doi.org/10.1098/rsta.2018.0242), metatorbernite amorphization wording varies among at 473 K, greater than 473 K, greater than 423 K and above 373 K; Figure S5 distinguishes a 423 K trace from a diffuse 473 K state. Metazeunerite high-temperature transformation is variously located at 473 K, above 373 K or 150 degrees C. Figure S9 supplies sampled states rather than a unique onset. The institutional PDF is marked For Review Only; use the published HTML and Royal Society supplement as the checked versions.

Acceptance:

- Acquire attributable temperature-labelled patterns, specimen-to-run mapping and any paired water-content measurements or author/publisher correction; do not silently choose one conflicting number.
- Retrieve crystallographic deposits through supported access and check that each file actually corresponds to the quoted sample/temperature before re-refinement or stronger structural claims.
- Keep natural air, natural vacuum and synthetic sealed-capillary arms distinct; preserve sampling intervals and uncertainty. No universal dehydration threshold, mineral-specific recovery or microbial activity follows from the current evidence.
- Any supported owner amendment requires canonical EDIT history and an independent successor scientific review. No author contact is authorized as a side effect of this issue.

source_issues.body:
The new florencite-(La) record retains natural identity without claiming a complete pure-La assay or an exact species-diagnostic Raman peak.

Ghignone et al. (2024), [DOI 10.1002/jrs.6640](https://doi.org/10.1002/jrs.6640), was inspected through the complete institutional article and publisher HTML. Table 1 identifies F1 as semiquantitative, unpolished/uncoated material with an oxide total of 35.6 wt%; it is not a complete bulk assay. Table 3 experimental columns are VS17 and F2, while nearby page 401 prose names F1. Section 4.3 gives 985 cm−1 for the main band, while Figure 3 labels 983 cm−1.

Acceptance: obtain original specimen-linked Raman/chemistry data or an attributable correction; trace the disputed columns to their specimens and reconcile peak assignments. Preserve semiquantitative limits. Do not infer an attachment exists from an unsuccessful guessed URL. Existing #317 concerns a different Ce-florencite treatment experiment. This is a source clarification, not an unresolved defect in the deliberately bounded owner.

source_issues.body:
The new monazite-(La) record accepts only La-labelled abiotic preparation evidence from Zhoujin et al. (2025), [DOI 10.1126/sciadv.adt3518](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.adt3518). Complete Europe PMC XML, original Figure 4 and the 24-page supplement were inspected.

Figure 4B supports synthetic La-rhabdophane conversion in 1 M H3PO4 at 210 °C for 1 h. Figure S7 separately shows LaCl3/LaF3 products, with 230 °C for 1 h in Methods. La starting amounts, independent replicate counts, quantitative purity and mass-balanced yields are not specified. The 100 mg loading, detailed pH series, in-situ onset and durability results are Nd-specific.

Separate Nd source-label conflicts: Table S4 lists pH 0.83 whereas Figure S11 says 0.65; Figures S18–S20 repeat the 6.38 caption although patterns/proportions differ. Their plots include Ti while Table S4 lists two mineral fractions, without an established normalization relation here.

Acceptance: recover La run sheets and precursor/direct-route lineage; obtain raw Nd pH/refinement assignments or an attributable correction. Do not import Nd loading, thresholds or leaching performance into La. Retain unresolved differences explicitly. The present owner is qualified; this is a source follow-up, not an uncorrected owner defect.

source_issues.body:
A microbial lead could extend monazite-(La), but no microbial claim was admitted because original methods and phase-identification evidence remain unverified.

Zhang et al. (2024), Enhancing La(III) biosorption and biomineralization with Micromonospora saelicesensis: Involvement of phosphorus and formation of monazite nano-minerals, [DOI 10.1016/j.scitotenv.2023.169851](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2023.169851), identifies strain KLBMP 9669 and claims LaPO4 nanoparticles in the preview/metadata. Publisher full/PDF routes returned HTTP 403; the Elsevier API returned metadata, not full text.

Acceptance: acquire legitimate full text and supplements. Verify biomass state, strain provenance, La substrate, phosphorus source, pH, time, loading, matched abiotic controls and replication. Inspect original TEM/SAED spacings against monazite, hydrated rhabdophane and alternatives. Nominal LaPO4 or La/P EDS alone is insufficient. Separate biosorption/solution depletion from phase-specific formation and isolated recovery before proposing any mechanism. Existing #130 and #133 concern different Ce/Sm experiments.

A separate 2026 M. auratinigra study, [DOI 10.1016/j.gca.2026.02.015](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gca.2026.02.015), and [Mendeley deposit](https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/wxdnxzm8g8/1) are forward leads, not substitute evidence for KLBMP 9669. Deposit files and data dictionary were not acquired in this pass. Keep strains and experiments separate.

source_issues.body:
Małecki and Gargul (2018), [DOI 10.3390/met8030177](https://doi.org/10.3390/met8030177), supports two abiotic laboratory routes for `data/records/spent-copper-zinc-alumina-catalyst.yaml`.

The sequential leach reports liquid/solid ratio 10 without units and a small H2O2 addition without concentration/dose. Its overall 97.5% Zn figure includes Zn retained in residue, whereas 61.9% is assigned to leachate. Residue XRD includes carbon and ZnAl2O4, so it is not an independently quantified pure product. For the melting arms, Table 1 Zn-dust values are unbalanced remainders; §3.2.1 says dust amount could not be identified and §5 describes estimation by difference. Fine fractions are not fully represented in the tabulated balance.

Acceptance: obtain attributable original experiment details or a legitimate correction for liquid/solid units, peroxide addition, fine/dust inventories and product/residue assay. Separate measured alloy metal, dissolved metal and retained residue from proposed recovery. Do not strengthen industrial, waste-free or overall isolated-product claims without a complete balance. Current narrow record retains these limitations; this issue is not an unresolved owner defect.

source_issues.body:
Farhan et al. (2026), [DOI 10.1038/s41598-026-47825-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-47825-8), describes laboratory leaching, settling and ethanol crystallization from a spent formaldehyde catalyst. Abstract A/O 1:2, Results-selected A/O 2, and Figure 5 time/speed/product A/O 1.5 disagree. NH4OH-to-(NH4)2SO4 versus NH3-to-NH4+ ratios are also interchanged although ammonium sulfate supplies two ammonium ions. About 92% leached in the summary differs from about 95% in the high-ratio arm. The 95.3% crystallization metric is liquor depletion, not feed-to-product overall yield; the >99.9% purity statement is linked to SEM-EDX without a separate bulk assay.

Russo et al. (2023), [DOI 10.1021/acssuschemeng.3c04318](https://doi.org/10.1021/acssuschemeng.3c04318), uses another feed and an abiotic tartaric-acid leach. Its printed efficiency equation omits explicit feed mass; the supporting TGA plot and 4.65% temperature-interval prose do not match clearly. The institutional PDF is typeset early-online pp. A-G; final numbered VOR remains a version follow-up. Downstream tartrate/ammonium-molybdate recovery is not quantitatively balanced.

Acceptance: obtain legitimate corrected methods/run data or attributable clarifications. Map buffer species/moles and A/O ratios to each experiment; establish initial/final volumes, collected-product quantities, uncertainty and bulk assay before recalculating overall recovery or purity. Preserve separate feeds and leaching versus crystallization denominators. Do not infer microbial activity from winery-derived acid or industrial deployment from feed origin. `data/records/spent-iron-molybdate-oxidation-catalyst.yaml` already retains these source limitations; this is a source follow-up, not an uncorrected record defect.
